CV02-q01-oh0g13: Never park with the hand valve; the air can leak off and the brakes let go.
Locked trailer brakes caused the skid; the hand valve makes it worse. Release the brakes instead.
CV02-q02-42yx0o: Those emergency brakes hold only while tank air lasts; it leaks away, so chock the wheels.
Never park with the hand valve; the air can leak off and the brakes release.
CV02-q03-5owphv: 60 to 80 psi isn't the handbook figure; the valve closes at about 20 to 45 psi.
100 to 125 psi is far too high; the valve closes when pressure falls to about 20 to 45 psi.
CV02-q04-e37r5r: Preventing wheel lockup is the job of ABS, not the tractor protection valve.
It does the opposite: it shuts air off to the trailer to save the tractor's own supply.
CV02-q05-c3na8g: The yellow diamond-shaped knob controls the parking brakes.
Blue marks the service line; the trailer air supply control is the red 8-sided knob.
CV02-q06-941s7g: Pushing the knob in sends air to the trailer; pulling it out shuts the air off.
The yellow diamond knob works the parking brakes; the red knob controls trailer air.
CV02-q07-kklwgo: Showing up only when you brake is the service-line leak pattern; losing the emergency line acts at once.
The valve closes, not opens, to keep the tractor's air, and the trailer emergency brakes come on.
CV02-q08-t2ybak: The knob popping out goes with emergency-line air loss; a service-line leak shows when you brake.
You'll likely notice it much sooner, as soon as you brake and tank pressure drops fast.
CV02-q09-qnwsm9: Control line is another name for the service line.
Signal line is another name for the service line.
CV02-q10-ytu9dk: The service line only signals how much braking; the emergency line fills the tanks.
Relay valves send tank air to the brakes; they don't fill the tanks.
CV02-q11-1hmggu: Glad hands aren't pushed straight together; hold them at 90 degrees, press the seals, then turn to lock.
Clean the couplers and seals before you connect them, not after.
CV02-q12-mm4dcg: The last trailer's rear shut-off valves should be closed anyway; crossed lines keep spring brakes on.
ABS doesn't release spring brakes; crossed lines send supply air into the service line instead.
CV02-q13-mqf8vv: Brakes staying locked happens with spring brakes; an old trailer with no tank air has no brakes at all.
The danger is on the trailer: with no spring brakes and no tank air, it has no brakes.
CV02-q14-vjqnao: Dummy couplers don't test anything; they're a place to hook hoses to keep out water and dirt.
Trailer air is stored in the trailer tanks; dummy couplers just keep unused lines clean.
CV02-q15-bkqt4y: Open valves at the very end of the rig let the air escape; close the last trailer's rear valves.
It's the reverse: all open, except closed at the back of the last trailer.
CV02-q16-93xr76: Pulling out the air supply knob does set the trailer emergency brakes.
A trailer that comes disconnected does get its emergency brakes set.
CV02-q17-ox1sp3: Trailer ABS lamps are yellow and on the left side, not red on the right.
Yellow is right, but the lamp goes on the left side, at a front or rear corner.
CV02-q18-n2n71f: ABS may not shorten your stop; it helps you keep control.
ABS doesn't add braking power; it works only when a wheel is about to lock.
CV02-q19-nbrh4x: Braking only the trailer can make it skid; the hand valve is only for testing.
Harder braking feeds the jackknife; ease off the brakes, if safe, to regain control.
CV02-dn-3g7kwe: Trailer emergency brakes come on when you pull the knob out, not push it in.
Parking brakes are the yellow diamond knob; the red knob controls trailer air.
CV02-dn-m672b4: The handbook names the lever positions "normal" and "emergency," not on and off.
Service and supply are air-line names, not lever positions.
CV02-dn-hwdcir: The trailer air supply is controlled by the red 8-sided knob.
The trailer hand valve (trolley valve) is a separate control that applies only the trailer brakes.
CV02-dn-ys4j4r: The supply line is only one of two; the service line runs between units too.
Control line is just another name for the service line, so there are only 2.
CV02-dn-t92ga8: Yellow isn't an air-line color; the yellow diamond is the parking brake knob.
CV02-dn-vx2gfu: Control line is another name for the service line.
Signal line is another name for the service line.
CV02-dn-n395do: Not 45 degrees; the couplers are held at 90 degrees to each other.
Not end to end; hold them at 90 degrees, press the seals together, then turn to lock.
CV02-dn-fd90d3: Automatic drains keep most moisture out, but you should still open the drains every day.
Don't wait for weak brakes; water and oil buildup can stop them working right, so drain daily.
CV02-dn-4hpogq: Open valves at the very end of the rig let the air escape; close the last trailer's rear valves.
The first trailer's rear valves must stay open to pass air back to the second trailer.
CV02-dn-0epjvc: March 1, 1998 is the trailer ABS date, not the spring-brake cutoff.
Being part of a double doesn't matter; the exemption is for dollies and pre-1975 trailers.
CV02-dn-p79vnm: 1975 is the spring-brake cutoff date, not the ABS date.
ABS is required on trailers and dollies built on or after March 1, 1998.
CV02-dn-6e62wy: Trailer ABS lamps are yellow, not red.
Blue marks the service line; trailer ABS lamps are yellow.
CV02-dn-84o4kv: The red 8-sided knob is the trailer air supply control in the cab, not a sign of trailer ABS.
Every combination has blue and red glad hands; they tell you nothing about ABS.
